data.question: Why does complete flag gates recorded after a kept-tree merge as stale?

evidence.note: complete and gate record now judge the same commit

chunk_findings.detail: `_landed_content` unconditionally rewrites both `tree_sha` and `source_tree` to the *landed commit's* values whenever `it.landed_after or it.merged_sha` is truthy, without ever checking that the tree it is measuring still equals that landed content. The worktree values just computed in `_measure` (`G.tree_fingerprint(wt)`, `G.source_tree(wt)`) are simply discarded. Concrete case: with `[worktree].remove_on_merge = false`, let the item land as commit `L`, then modify a tracked source file in the kept worktree (uncommitted) before running a gate — a dirty kept tree is a state the new regression test already declares normal, since it tolerates an extra scratch file there. `ddflow critic` (or rubber_duck/standards) then runs on `L+mod`, but `_measure` records `tree_sha = "L[:12]+clean"` and the landed `source_tree`. At `complete`, the expected value is derived from the same landed commit, so the gate matches and is reported fresh, whereas before this change the recorded fingerprint was the kept tree's (dirty/different) one and the gate was flagged stale. The post-merge gate that actually executed never saw `L` at all; if `mod` is later dropped, `L` is completed with a "post-merge pass" that in fact only covered a different tree. Guarding the substitution with a content check (`G.source_tree(wt) == G.commit_source_tree(repo, landed)`) before replacing `tree_sha`/`source_tree` would keep the Bb47a48b173 fix without converting a real tree mismatch into a false pass.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gates.py `_landed_content` / `_measure`

chunk_findings.detail:
`_landed_content` unconditionally substitutes the landed commit's measurement for any recorded gate once `it.landed_after or it.merged_sha` is set, hard-coding the tree fingerprint as `f"{landed[:12]}+clean"` and `source_tree` as the landed commit's source. This assumes the kept worktree (`remove_on_merge=false`) is at the landed commit modulo untracked files, but it does not check the worktree's tracked state. The gate is actually executed in that kept worktree, so if the worktree has any *tracked* modification, the gate validates content that never landed, yet the recorded evidence now claims it validated the clean landed tree.

Concrete repro: `config worktree.remove_on_merge false`; let a gate pass in the item tree; merge; edit a tracked file in the kept tree; run a second gate (e.g. `standards`, `cwd = "worktree"`) that passes; run `complete`. Before this change, `_measure` recorded `G.tree_fingerprint(wt)` (`<landed>+dirty`) and `source_tree` of the modified tree, so `completion._tree_being_completed` — which expects `<landed>+clean` — flagged the evidence as "passed on a different tree". After the change, `measured.update(_landed_content(...))` overwrites both fields with the clean landed values, so the comparison matches and the stale note is silently suppressed, accepting a gate result that was produced against unreviewed content. The untracked-scratch case this change targets and the tracked-modification case are indistinguishable here because cleanliness is never consulted; the fix should only attribute the gate to the landed commit when the kept tree's tracked content still equals it (e.g. drop the `+clean`/source substitution when the fingerprint reports dirty), otherwise it trades the reported false positive for a false negative in the same evidence check.

chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gates.py:_landed_content

chunk_findings.detail:
The function picks one of two different identity representations for the same kept tree depending on the untracked state *at measurement time*: when tracked content matches the landing and the worktree differs only by untracked files it returns the landed commit id (`landed[:12]+clean`); when `source == here` it returns `{}` and leaves `measured["tree_sha"]` as the worktree's own id (`W`). Because gates are recorded and `complete` re-measures at two different moments, the two sides only agree if the untracked set happens to be identical at both moments — and a scratch file is by definition transient.

Concrete failure: `worktree.remove_on_merge = false`, land `T1` and let the gates/pipeline run while the kept tree has no untracked files (recorded `tree_sha = W`, the worktree id — pre-fix the false positive and the pristine control show `W != <landed>+clean`); then `touch scratch.txt` in the kept tree (untracked, never landed) and run `ddflow complete T1`. At complete time `G.source_tree(wt)` now differs from the landed source, the new branch is taken, and complete measures the tree as `<landed>+clean` (`L`), which differs from the recorded `W` — so `complete` prints "passed on a different tree" for gates on a tree whose tracked content never changed. The reverse ordering fails identically: gates recorded while the scratch file exists (recorded `L`) and the scratch file removed before `complete` (complete measures `W`) produce the same false stale note. This is exactly the false positive bug Bb47a48b173 is supposed to close; the change only fixes it for the case where the untracked state is unchanged between the last gate and `complete` (which is why the probe, and the new committed-work test, both pass). The fix needs to base the recorded identity on a value that is stable across both measurements (e.g. always record the worktree id and have `complete` apply the "only-untracked" rule to the gate side too), rather than on a snapshot of the untracked set taken at reco

chunk_findings.detail: The only case this helper is written to forgive — a kept tree whose tracked content equals what landed but which also holds untracked scratch — is precisely the case that reaches this final `return`: `here = G.source_tree(wt)` is the worktree's own content id (the scratch it is supposed to tolerate is in it, which is why the branch exists at all), so `source == here` is false, `entries` minus `_untracked_paths(wt)` is exactly the landed content, and the helper hands back `tree_sha = f"{landed[:12]}+clean"` plus `G.commit_source_tree(repo, landed)`. That is byte-for-byte the value the unfixed `_landed_content` produced and that the bug report identifies as the cause: for a kept tree (`remove_on_merge = false`) `complete` compares each gate's recorded `tree_sha` against the tree it is completing (`G.tree_sha(wt)`, i.e. the kept tree's own head+clean), so re-supplying the landed commit's sha cannot make the post-merge gates match — the false "passed on a different tree" note is still printed. Concretely, in the regression scenario (`test_an_untracked_file_left_in_a_kept_tree_does_not_make_the_evidence_stale`: scratch file left in the kept tree, `pass_pipeline(..., omit=("unit_tests","merge"))` recording critic/rubber_duck/standards after the merge, then `complete T1`) the helper takes the final return and `assert NOTE not in out + err` fails; the fix only takes effect through the earlier `source == here` guard, which fires only when untracked files do not perturb `G.source_tree(wt)` — and in that case the untracked-file handling in the branch is unreachable dead logic and the docstring's stated leniency ("differs … ONLY by untracked files … is measured as what landed") is never actually implemented. Either way, the branch that is supposed to address the untracked case either never runs or re-emits the value `complete` rejects for kept trees.
